questions.question: Which of statement is **NOT correct** regarding the earthquake waves?

options.text: P-wave can travel through only solid and liquid mediums but not gaseous mediums.
S-waves is that they can travel only through solid materials.
P-waves move faster and are the first to arrive at the surface.
P-waves are called the primary waves.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seismic Waves (Earthquake Waves)****​**

 
 
• Seismic waves are waves of energy caused by earthquakes or an explosion. They are the energy that travels through the earth and is recorded on seismographs.
 
• Earthquake waves are basically of two types — body waves and surface waves.
 
• Body waves are generated due to the release of energy at the focus and move in all directions traveling through the body of the earth. Hence, the name body waves.
 
 
 
• There are two types of body waves. They are called P and S-waves.
 
 
• ​P-waves move faster and are the first to arrive at the surface. **Hence**, **Statement 3 is correct**.
 
• These are also called ‘primary waves’. Hence, Statement 4 is correct
 
• The P-waves are similar to sound waves. 
 
• They travel through gaseous, liquid, and solid materials. Hence, Statement 1 is not correct.
 
• P-waves are also called the longitudinal waves.
 
• The seismographs located beyond 145° from epicenters; record the arrival of P-waves, but not that of S-waves.
 
• P-waves create density differences in the material leading to stretching (rarefaction) and squeezing (compression) of the material.
 
• S-waves arrive at the surface with some time lag. These are called secondary waves.
 
• An important fact about S-waves is that they can travel only through solid materials. Hence, Statement 2 is correct.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There exist some specific areas where the waves are not reported. Such a zone is called the ‘shadow zone’.
 
• A zone between 105° and 145° from the epicenter was identified as the shadow zone for both types of waves.
 
• The shadow zone of the S-wave is much larger than that of the P-wave.
 
• The shadow zone of S-waves is not only larger in extent but it is also a little over 40 percent of the earth's surface.

4f

questions.question: Beta-carotene, lycopene, lutein and selenium are examples of:

• Beta-carotene, lycopene, lutein, and selenium are examples of an antioxidant.
 
• An antioxidant is a thing that prevents other molecules from being oxidized; it shields the body against free radicals.

questions.question: One may be tempted to treat higher level of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country as an index of greater well-being of the people of that country. But there are some reasons due to which this may not be correct. Which of the following is NOT one of these reasons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1. ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Level of Political Awareness (Correct Answer): The level of political awareness is not typically considered a reason for treating a higher level of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) as an inaccurate indicator of greater well-being.
 
 
• Political awareness is more related to the political engagement and consciousness of the population, while GDP is primarily an economic indicator.
 
 
 
• Non-monetary Exchanges: One reason why GDP may not accurately reflect well-being is the exclusion of non-monetary exchanges.
 
 
• GDP focuses on market transactions and does not account for non-market activities like household work, volunteering, or informal exchanges, which contribute significantly to well-being but are not monetized.
 
 
 
• Distribution of GDP: The distribution of GDP matters because even if a country has a high overall GDP, the benefits may not be evenly distributed among the population.
 
 
• Income inequality can lead to disparities in well-being, with certain groups experiencing higher living standards than others.
 
 
 
• Externalities: GDP does not account for externalities, which are the unintended side effects of economic activities.
 
 
• Positive externalities, such as education and healthcare, and negative externalities, like pollution and environmental degradation, can impact well-being but are not fully captured by GDP.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP): GDP is a measure of the total economic output of a country.
 
• It includes the value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders over a specific period.
 
• While GDP is a widely used indicator for the overall economic performance of a country, it has limitations when it comes to assessing the well-being of individuals.

questions.question: Who was the leader of Kheda Satyagraha that was launched against the government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****__Mahatma Gandhi.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kheda Satyagraha **was a significant movement launched in **1918** in the** Kheda district of Gujarat**, India, against the oppressive policies of the British government regarding the payment of land revenue.
 
• The farmers in Kheda were facing severe crop failures and were unable to pay the land revenue due to natural calamities. 
 
• About** Kheda Satyagraha** - 
 
 
• The Kheda Satyagraha of 1918, initiated on March 11, unfolded in the Kheda District of Gujarat, part of the Bombay province during that period. 
 
• Initially organized by peasants, particularly the Patidar community, and spearheaded by local leader** Mohanlal Pandya**, the movement gained prominence under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It Marked the first non-cooperation movement by the masses.
 
• The region faced a bad harvest in 1917–18, compounded by soaring prices of essentials. The outbreak of severe plague in 1918 led to significant deaths in Gujarat, particularly in Kheda.
 
• The British government raised taxes by 23% in the Bombay Presidency, aggravating the plight of the peasants.
 
• The peasants petitioned for a reduction in land revenue, invoking the government's famine code, but their plea was rejected.
 
• Local leaders like Mohanlal Pandya initiated a no-revenue campaign in November 1917.
 
• Seeking assistance from outside leaders, they reached out to the Gujarat Sabha in Ahmedabad, including Mahatma Gandhi, who advised firmness in their demands.
 
• The Gujarat Sabha urged the Bombay government for exemptions and postponement of revenue demands, but receiving no favorable response, encouraged peasants not to pay land revenues.
 
• Gandhi arrived in Bombay in February 1918 and, accompanied by Gujarat Sabha members, visited Kheda villages to assess the peasants' suffering.
 
• Finding justification for the peasants' demand to suspend revenue collection, Gandhi decided to resort to Satyagraha.
 
• At a meeting in Nadiad on March 22, 1918, Gandhi urged volunteers to take a sacred pledge not to pay the assessment for the year, wholly or in part.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT antimicrobial drugs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Antacids.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Antacids are not antimicrobial drugs.

 
 
• Antacids are not antimicrobial drugs. Instead, they are medications that neutralize excess stomach acid to relieve symptoms of indigestion, heartburn, or acid reflux.
 
• They do not directly target microorganisms but rather work on the acidity level in the stomach.
 
• Common antacids include substances like calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, and aluminum hydroxide.
 
 
 
• **Antibiotics -** 
 
 
• Antibiotics are antimicrobial drugs that specifically target and kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria.
 
• They are used to treat bacterial infections and work by interfering with bacterial processes, such as cell wall synthesis or protein production.
 
• Examples include penicillin, tetracycline, and amoxicillin.
 
 
 
• **​****Antiseptics **- 
 
 
• ​Antiseptics are substances applied to living tissues, such as skin, to reduce the risk of infection.
 
• Unlike disinfectants, antiseptics are safe for use on living tissues and are used to clean wounds, cuts, and surgical sites.
 
• Examples include iodine, hydrogen peroxide, and rubbing alcohol.
 
 
 
• **Disinfectants** - 
 
 
• ​Disinfectants are chemical substances used to eliminate or reduce the number of microorganisms on surfaces and inanimate objects.
 
• They are not typically used on living tissues but are effective against bacteria, viruses, and fungi.
 
• Common disinfectants include bleach, hydrogen peroxide, and alcohol-based solutions.

questions.question: Martyrdom of revolutionary ___________ took place on 27 February, 1931.

• **About Chandrashekhar Azad** 

 
 
• Chandrashekhar Azad was a fearless freedom fighter known for his role in the Kakori Conspiracy and other revolutionary activities.
 
• Azad was a key member of the HSRA and played a crucial role in planning and executing acts against the British government.
 
• His commitment to the cause was unwavering, and he preferred to die fighting rather than being captured by the British. He shot himself during a confrontation in Alfred Park, Allahabad, on **27 February 1931. **
 
 
 
• **​Batukeshwar Dutt **
 
 
• **​**Batukeshwar Dutt was a revolutionary who actively participated alongside Bhagat Singh in the protest against repressive laws by bombing the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929.
 
• He, along with Bhagat Singh, intentionally courted arrest to use the trial as a platform to promote their revolutionary ideals and criticize British imperialism.
 
• Dutt's act of nonviolent protest through hunger strikes during imprisonment became significant in the narrative of the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Sachindranath Sanyal **
 
 
• Sachindranath Sanyal was a key revolutionary and a mentor to many freedom fighters during the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was one of the founding members of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), which later became the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
 
• Sanyal was instrumental in organizing and guiding revolutionary activities, including the Kakori Conspiracy of 1925.
 
• His role was crucial in shaping the ideology and strategy of the HSRA, which aimed at overthrowing British rule through armed struggle.
 
 
 
• Bhagat Singh
 
 
• Bhagat Singh was a prominent revolutionary and a charismatic leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He gained fame for his role in the protest against the Simon Commission and the bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929.
 
• Bhagat Singh, along with Rajguru and Sukhdev, was sentenced to death in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.
 
• Their execution on 23 March 1931 galvanized public opinion and contributed significantly to the anti-colonial sentiment in India.

questions.question: Which cyber security measure involves verifying the identity of users before granting access to a system or network?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Multi-factor authentication.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Authentication protocols **can go further than **2FA **and **use multiple factors **to **authenticate a person or system**.
 
• **Authentication **methods that use **two or more factors **are called ***multifactor authentication (MFA).***
 
• **Authentication **is the process of *determining whether someone or something is who or what they say they are*.
 
• Authentication technology provides access control for systems by checking to see if a user's credentials match the credentials in a database of authorized users or a data authentication server.
 
• **There are several authentication types. **
 
• For user identity, users are typically identified with a **user ID**; authentication occurs when the user provides *credentials, such as a password, that match their user ID*.
 
• ***The practice of requiring a user ID and password is known as single-factor authentication (SFA). ***
 
• In recent years, organizations have strengthened authentication by asking for additional authentication factors.
 
• ***These can be a unique code provided to a user over a mobile device when a sign-on is attempted or a biometric signature, such as a facial scan or thumbprint. ***
 
• ***This is known as two-factor authentication (2FA).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Firewall configuration:**__

__
 
• **Firewall configuration **is a crucial aspect of **network security**.
 
• It involves adjusting the settings of a **firewall **to determine which **data packets **are allowed into a **network **and which ones are not.
 
• This is done by **manipulating factors **such as **domain names **and **Internet Protocol (IP) **addresses to ensure optimal protection of a network.
 
• **A firewall **can exist as a **hardware device **or **software **running on a **third-party operating system**.
 
• Regardless of its form, it controls the **flow of traffic across a network**.

**Regular software updates:**__

__
 
• **Regular software **updates are **fundamental to maintaining **a **smooth-running **and **secure software system**.
 
• These updates often include solutions to various issues that were present in the previous versions of the software, as well as offering improvements or additional features.
 
• 
 
**Software updates can include:**__

 
 
• 
 
__**Bug Fixes: **__

 __
 
• Often updates include **"bug fixes**", or **corrections for problems **experienced in the **software's performance**.
 
• An example of this would be a situation where an ***application crashes unexpectedly***.
 
• A software update could involve a bug fix that "**improves the ability to switch apps, reducing unexpected software crashes**".
 
 
 
• 
 
**Feature Enhancements: **Some updates may come with improved features or new capabilities added to the software, which can enhance user experience.

 
 
• 
 
**Security Improvements:**

 
 
• In this evolving **digital landscape**, **maintaining secure software is critical**.
 
• Regular updates often incorporate **security patches **or ***improvements to better protect against evolving cybersecurity threats.***
 
 

**Network encryption:**__

__
 
• **Network encryption **is a crucial aspect of **network security **that helps **safeguard information **by **converting understandable data **into an **unreadable format**.
 
• This conversion** **is done using an **encryption algorithm **and a ***randomly generated encryption key***.
 
• The scrambled data, known as ***ciphertext, ***is only **readable **when **it's decrypted **using the ***corresponding decryption key***.
 
• **Purpose**__:
 __
 
• **The primary purpose **of **network encryption **is to **ensure privacy and security**.
 
• Only the **intended recipient **or the **rightful data owner **can **decipher encrypted communications or data**, preventing parties such as ***attackers, ad networks, Internet service providers, and even governments ***from intercepting and reading the sensitive data.
 
• **This effectively protects user privacy.**
 
 
 
• **Types of Network Encryption**__:
 __
 
• One of the encryption types is the **Triple Data Encryption Standard (3DES), **a version of the **original DES encryption algorithm**.
 
• **The 3DES encrypts data three times **using **three 64-bit keys**, resulting in a **key length of 192 bits**.
 
• Being a **symmetric encryption, **the **encryption and decryption keys in 3DES **are the same, and therefore, **private**.
 
• **Moreover, it encrypts data in 64-bit segments.**
 
 
 
• **Importance**__:
 
 
• **Network encryption **plays a crucial role **in maintaining the confidentiality of data transported across networks.**
 
• It helps **protect sensitive corporate and personal information during transmission**, thus making a significant contribution to **integrity and trust in digital communications.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a common condition that develops when a sticky substance called plaque accumulates inside your arteries, causing them to harden and narrow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Atherosclerosis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Atherosclerosis, sometimes called "hardening of the arteries," occurs when fat, cholesterol and other substances build up in the walls of arteries.
 
• These deposits are called plaques. Over time, these plaques can narrow or completely block the arteries and cause problems throughout the body.
 
• High-fat diet, smoking, and obesity can cause atherosclerosis
 
• Coronary Artery Disease, often referred to as atherosclerosis, affects the vessels that supply blood to the heart muscle.
 
• It is caused by deposits of calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissues, which make the lumen of arteries narrower.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__ Multiple sclerosis:__

__
 
• Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune inflammatory disease
 
• It affects the central nervous system's white matter
 
• It is mainly characterized by a relapsing or progressive course.
 
• Characterized by the appearance of patches of demyelination in the white matter of the CNS, generally starting in the optic nerve, spinal cord, or cerebellum.
 
• The myelin sheaths degenerate and the myelin is removed by the microglial cells. Astrocytes proliferate leading to the formation of the gliotic scar.
 
• As demyelination occurs the conduction of the nerve impulses in the axons is slowed and altered.

**Hyperaldosteronism:**__

__
 
• The pathobiological effects of **hyperaldosteronism **on the cardiovascular system extend beyond increased intravascular fluid retention and volume overload.
 
• **Hyperaldosteronism **causes endothelial dysfunction and **impairs vascular reactivity, **in part, by decreasing *vascular antioxidant capacity, increasing oxidant stress, and limiting bioavailable nitric oxide.*
 
• **Hyperaldosteronism** also activates inflammation; alters fibrinolysis by increasing plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 expression; and promotes tissue fibrosis.
 
• Other adverse effects attributed to **hyperaldosteronism **that may influence cardiovascular function include sympathetic nervous system activation, decreased baroreceptor sensitivity, increased electrolyte excretion **(K+, Mg+), and cardiomyocyte apoptosis.**

**Hypervitaminosis:**__

 
• It is a condition in which vitamins are stored in the body at a high level.
 
• Signs and symptoms of Hypervitaminosis:
 
 
• Frequent urination and increased urine amount.
 
• Irregular heartbeat.
 
• Bones and joint pain.
 
• Muscles pain
 
• Stone formation in the urinary tract.
 
 
 
• People who get little or no **vitamin** **C **(below about 10 mg per day) for many weeks can get scurvy.
 
• Scurvy causes ***fatigue, inflammation of the gums, small red or purple spots on the skin, joint pain, poor wound healing, and corkscrew hairs.***

__

• It is one of the rarest elements in the Earth's crust.

• It is the eighth most abundant element in the Earth's crust, and the third most plentiful element dissolved in seawater.
 
• Magnesium is used in dietary supplements, as an additive agent in conventional propellants, as a reducing agent for the production of uranium and other metals from their salts, and to produce magnesium carbonate for the ceramic industry

questions.question: How much of global trade is carried out through the sea route?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**90%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the International Maritime Organization (IMO), up to 90% of the world's goods are transported through maritime trade**.
 
• Sea routes offer an efficient and cost-effective mode of transportation, especially for heavy and bulky cargo, like minerals, crude oil, and other commodities.
 
• It has a significant impact on the global economy, as the trade through sea route is essential for the bulk transport of raw materials, and the import/export of affordable food and goods.
 
• Efficient maritime trade relies on elements like advanced naval technology, infrastructure at ports, legal frameworks for trade, and maritime security.
 
• The industry is witnessing technological advancements, from larger, energy-efficient vessels to digitalization initiatives improving cargo tracking and port operations.
 
• However, maritime trade also has its challenges like piracy, geopolitical conflicts, environmental concerns due to pollution and the introduction of alien species through ballast water, and operational issues like cargo damage and delays present ongoing difficulties.
 
• The maritime industry is also an important source of jobs and contributes heavily to reducing global poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Here are some of the world's most important maritime trade routes:
 
 
• **The Panama Canal Route**: Connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean via the Panama Canal, allowing ships to bypass the lengthy Cape Horn route around South America.
 
• **The Suez Canal Route**: Connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through the Suez Canal, providing a shortcut from the North Atlantic to the Indian Ocean.
 
• **The Strait of Malacca Route**: It is one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, linking the Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean.
 
• **The Straits of Hormuz Route**: A crucial passageway connecting the Persian Gulf to the Arabian Sea. It is strategically important because of the oil trade.
 
• **Trans-Pacific Route**: It's the primary shipping route between Asia and the West Coast of North America.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols is used by email clients to send email to mail servers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SMTP**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SMTP, or Simple Mail Transfer Protocol**, is a **standard protocol for sending emails on the Internet**.
 
• SMTP servers have a set of rules that the email clients follow to send mail.
 
• SMTP is primarily used for outgoing mail, while other protocols such as IMAP or POP3 are used to download incoming mail from a mail server.
 
• Established as an Internet standard in the 1980s, SMTP is designed to send, receive, and relay outgoing mail between email senders and receivers.
 
• SMTP works in conjunction with protocols such as POP3 and IMAP by sending the outgoing mail that the other protocols have downloaded.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **TCP/IP**

 
 
• TCP/IP, or Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol, is a suite of communication protocols used to interconnect network devices on the Internet.
 
• It is not specifically designed to send emails.
 
• TCP/IP forms the backbone of all modern internet including email transmission, but the actual protocol used by email clients for sending email is SMTP.
 
 
 
• **IMAP**
 
 
• IMAP, or Internet Message Access Protocol, is another protocol for email retrieval.
 
• Unlike SMTP, it is primarily used for receiving emails, not sending them.
 
• IMAP allows an email client to access email on a remote mail server, usually storing messages on the server, allowing the user to view and manage the messages as though they were stored locally.
 
 
 
• **POP3**
 
 
• POP3, or Post Office Protocol version 3, is used to retrieve emails from a mail server.
 
• Similar to IMAP, it is used for receiving emails, not sending them.
 
• The main difference between POP3 and IMAP is that POP3 downloads the email from the server to the device, and then deletes the email from the server.
 
• This makes managing email across multiple devices more difficult than IMAP which keeps emails on the server allowing access across multiple devices.

• **Marwar Plateau**:

 
 
• The Marwar Plateau, also known as the **Mewar Plateau**, is part of the** larger Peninsular Plateau** of India.
 
• It's located in the Marwar region of **Rajasthan**, predominantly in the **western part** of the state.
 
• Characterized by undulating terrain, the plateau is** largely composed** of **compact crystalline rocks**.
 
• It lacks **rich, fertile soil and irrigation** facilities, and as such, is **not ideal** for **productive farming**.

• ​The **Malwa Plateau** is a region in **north-central India**, predominantly encompassing **central Madhya Pradesh State** and southeastern Rajasthan.
 
• It is bounded by the** Madhya Bharat Plateau **and **Bundelkhand Upland** to the north, the **Vindhya Range** to the **east** and south, and the **Gujarat Plains** to the west.
 
• This plateau region is of **volcanic origin**.
 
• Despite being a plateau, it has a **diverse biome**, including **teak forests** and **fertile black soil **suitable for **cotton cultivation** in some areas.

• This plateau has been formed by continental uplift from forces deep within the Earth.
 
• The **Gondwana** substrates of the plateau speak to its **ancient origins**.
 
• It is rich in **mineral resources**, including **coal, iron, bauxite, and mica**, leading it to be heavily industrialized.

• **Much like** the **Chota Nagpur Plateau**, it also formed from **forces deep within the planet's crust** that led to uplift.
 
• Predominantly a highland region, the **topography** of the Chhattisgarh Plateau is marked by** hills, plains, and river valleys**.
